content: The protein KIBRA, also referred to as kidney and brain expressed protein or WW domain-containing protein 1 (WWC1), is encoded by the WWC1 gene in humans. A single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP), identified as rs17070145, within the WWC1 gene has been linked to human memory performance in a study conducted in 2006. However, a subsequent study in 2008 involving 584 participants did not find significant evidence to support the association between KIBRA and memory. Despite this, the findings of the original 2006 study were replicated in a smaller sample of elderly individuals in 2008. Further research in 2009, conducted on two large UK cohorts, suggested that KIBRA is specifically associated with the forgetting of non-semantic material. Additionally, investigations have begun to explore the potential role of KIBRA in the pathophysiology of Alzheimer’s disease. KIBRA has been identified to interact with at least 10 other proteins, including synaptopodin, protein kinase C zeta (PKCζ), and dendrin. Many of these interaction partners are involved in the regulation of synaptic plasticity. For example, dendrin is a post-synaptic protein whose expression is influenced by sleep deprivation. Furthermore, KIBRA has been demonstrated to interact with protein kinase M zeta (PKMζ).
